html:
The Battle of Tsushima was fought on 27 and 28 May 1905 in the strait between Korea and Japan. The Japanese fleet under Admiral Togo Heihachiro destroyed the Russian fleet in one of the most complete naval victories in history.

In the Russo-Japanese War, Japan's navy had bottled up Russia's Pacific ships. Russia sent its Baltic fleet under Admiral Zinovy Rozhestvensky around Africa to help, a voyage of about 33,000 km that took seven months. By the time it arrived, Port Arthur had fallen, so it made for Vladivostok through the Tsushima Strait. Togo was waiting. His ships were faster and their crews better trained. He crossed in front of the Russian line and smashed its leading battleships with gunfire. That night torpedo boats attacked the survivors. Russia lost 21 ships sunk and about 5,000 men killed. Japan lost three torpedo boats and 117 men.

The tsar agreed to peace talks, which ended in the Treaty of Portsmouth. The defeat fed the revolution of 1905 in Russia. Japan became a great naval power and took over Korea in 1910. Navies everywhere drew the lesson that big guns at long range decide battles.
